questions.prompt: Which description best fits an abjad such as the basic Arabic writing system?

choices.text: Each sign normally represents a whole word
Consonants are primary, with vowels often omitted or marked separately
Every sign represents one complete syllable
Letter shapes directly depict the things named

questions.hint: Consider the difference between the main letters and optional vowel marks.
questions.explanation: An abjad principally represents consonants. Vowels may be omitted or indicated through additional devices.

questions.prompt: What is the rebus principle in writing?

choices.text: Using colour to mark grammatical tense
Arranging text to resemble its subject
Using a pictured object's name for its sound value
Assigning every word a unique numeral

questions.hint: A drawing of an eye can contribute to writing a sentence unrelated to vision.
questions.explanation: The rebus principle uses a sign's pronunciation to represent another word or syllable with a similar sound.

questions.prompt: In Devanagari, what does a virama normally indicate?

choices.text: The absence of a consonant's inherent vowel
The end of a complete sentence
A change from present to past tense

questions.hint: The basic consonant sign otherwise includes more than a consonant sound.
questions.explanation: A virama suppresses the inherent vowel associated with a consonant; it also participates in forming consonant clusters.

questions.prompt: Why is Hangul alphabetic even though its text is arranged in syllable blocks?

choices.text: Every block has an unrelated, indivisible shape
Its component letters represent consonants and vowels
Each block represents a word independently of pronunciation
It uses the Latin alphabet inside each block

questions.hint: Distinguish a unit's visual grouping from what its internal parts encode.
questions.explanation: Hangul groups letters into syllable blocks, but the component jamo represent consonants and vowels.

questions.prompt: In a Chinese phono-semantic compound character, what roles do the two main components typically serve?

choices.text: One marks tense and the other marks number
One gives stroke order and the other gives punctuation
One suggests meaning and the other suggests pronunciation
One gives a translation and the other gives a page reference

questions.hint: The character combines different kinds of clues; historical sound changes can weaken one of them.
questions.explanation: A phono-semantic compound pairs a semantic component with a phonetic component. Neither guarantees a complete modern definition or exact modern pronunciation.
